gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that the one wireless board under $50, the Gamakay NS68 tri-mode ($39.99, $3.20 over the wired one), keeps 8,000 Hz only on the cable: 0.125 ms per report wired against 1 ms on wireless, 8 times longer.
standout_why: Compared against six opened pages. hlplanet.com (cited) lists the NS68 at $42.99 as 'wired or wireless, extremely cheap' with no polling, scan or rapid-trigger figure. mechanicalkeyboard.net's HE68 Lite review (cited) already converts 8,000 Hz to 0.125 ms and 1,000 Hz to 1 ms, but for a wired-only board, so the conversion itself is not new. chronicreload.com, deal.ai's under-$50 list and computerstationnation.com give no wireless figure and no rapid-trigger step count. Two limits keep this at 1: PC Gamer's guide (cited) and its NS68 review came back truncated, so I could not check what they say; and gamepadsquire.com's NS68 review (its guide was result 10, which I did not open) already carries 1,000 Hz wireless, 32,000 Hz scan and about 40 h battery, so that guide may hold part of this.
decides: It confirms the NS68 as the row we can link under $50 (awin:gamakay, no record yet; every keyboard we already list is over $50, the NS75 nearest) and splits it by variant rather than changing the pick. The wired NS68 at $36.79 gives the same 0.125 ms report interval as the 8K rivals ChatGPT named. The tri-mode at $39.99 wins only the 'wireless under $50' segment, and the page must say its wireless modes run at 1 ms per report. The scan-rate figure removes one reason to prefer the HE68 Lite: 128 kHz against 32 kHz is worth at most 0.023 ms. Both rest on reviewer figures, not Gamakay's own page, which returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. I could not verify the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro, ChatGPT's top pick, at all, so this angle cannot say the NS68 beats it.

findings.label: Time per report, cable vs wireless
findings.value: 0.125 ms wired (8,000 Hz); 1 ms wireless (1,000 Hz); 8 times longer
findings.source_title: GAMAKAY x Naugh Shark NS68 Review (Crafting Worlds, Tristan)
findings.note: Crafting Worlds: 'up to 8000Hz in wired mode', 'Wireless is limited to 1000Hz'. Arithmetic: 1,000 ms / 8,000 = 0.125 ms; 1,000 ms / 1,000 = 1 ms; 1 / 0.125 = 8. GamePadSquire's review gives the same two rates. Neither separates 2.4 GHz from Bluetooth. Reviewer figures: Gamakay's page was not readable (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Price of adding wireless
findings.source_title: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 Hall Effect Magnetic keyboard 8K Polling Rate 0.01mm RT Accuracy
findings.note: Prices are the brief's partner-store read of 2026-11-21 (wired white, side-printed keycaps $36.79; tri-mode white, shine-through keycaps $39.99), used as given. I did not re-open the page: storecheck and WebFetch returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. Arithmetic: 39.99 - 36.79 = 3.20; 3.20 / 36.79 = 8.7%. The two variants also differ in keycaps. Sale prices; the brief gives the sale end as 2026-11-30.

findings.label: Room left under the $50 budget
findings.source_title: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 Hall Effect Magnetic keyboard 8K Polling Rate 0.01mm RT Accuracy
findings.note: Arithmetic: 50 - 36.79 = 13.21; 50 - 39.99 = 10.01. Same brief-supplied prices as above, not re-opened by me. Sale prices through 2026-11-30.

findings.label: Price per key
findings.value: $0.54 per key wired; $0.59 per key tri-mode
findings.source_title: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 Review (GamePadSquire Test Desk, updated 2026-08-09)
findings.note: Key count of 68 from GamePadSquire; prices from the brief's partner read of 2026-11-21. Arithmetic: 36.79 / 68 = 0.541; 39.99 / 68 = 0.588. The summary I got of GamePadSquire's page showed about $0.59 per key at $39.99; I could not tell whether the page prints that figure or my reader computed it.

findings.label: Rapid trigger steps across the key's travel
findings.value: 350 steps (3.5 mm travel at 0.01 mm resolution)
findings.source_title: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 Review (GamePadSquire Test Desk, updated 2026-08-09)
findings.note: GamePadSquire: Outemu Peach Crystal switch, 3.5 mm total travel, 0.01 mm rapid trigger resolution. Arithmetic: 3.5 / 0.01 = 350. The 0.01 mm figure also appears in Gamakay's product title.

findings.label: Rapid trigger steps across the key's travel
findings.value: 172 steps (3.44 mm at 0.02 mm), about half the NS68's 350
findings.source_title: Best Budget Hall Effect Keyboards in 2026 (Under $50) | Chronic Reload
findings.note: Chronic Reload lists 0.02 mm RT step distance and a 0.02-3.44 mm range. Arithmetic: 3.44 / 0.02 = 172. It gives the same 0.02 mm step for the WIN60 HE but no travel figure. Aula's own page was not readable (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Rapid trigger steps across the adjustable range
findings.value: 34 steps (3.4 mm at 0.1 mm), a step 10 times coarser than the NS68's 0.01 mm
findings.source_title: Best Budget Hall Effect Keyboards in 2026 (Under $50) | Chronic Reload
findings.note: Chronic Reload lists 0.1 mm 'RT accuracy', 0.1-3.4 mm and 61 keys. Arithmetic: 3.4 / 0.1 = 34; 0.1 / 0.01 = 10. Chronic Reload uses 'RT accuracy' and 'RT step distance' interchangeably, and I did not open Redragon's page, so verify there before this decides anything.

findings.label: Actuation steps across the adjustable range
findings.value: 330 steps (0.1 to 3.4 mm in 0.01 mm steps)
findings.source_title: Epomaker HE68 Lite Review 2026: Best $50 Hall Effect Keyboard?
findings.note: Arithmetic: (3.4 - 0.1) / 0.01 = 330. This is the actuation-point step; the review states no separate rapid trigger minimum. It also lists 68 keys, wired only, 8,000 Hz and 128 kHz scan as the maker's specification.

findings.label: What a 128 kHz scan rate buys over 32 kHz
findings.value: 0.023 ms at most, under a fifth of one 8,000 Hz report (0.125 ms)
findings.source_title: Epomaker HE68 Lite Review 2026: Best $50 Hall Effect Keyboard?
findings.note: HE68 Lite 128 kHz from this review (maker spec); NS68 32,000 Hz from GamePadSquire's NS68 review (https://gamepadsquire.com/keyboards/gamakay-x-naughshark-ns68/, read 2026-11-21). Arithmetic: 1,000 / 32,000 = 0.031 ms per scan; 1,000 / 128,000 = 0.008 ms; 0.031 - 0.008 = 0.023 ms; 0.023 / 0.125 = 19%. The NS68 scan rate is a reviewer's figure, not read from Gamakay.

findings.label: Days between charges at a stated daily use
findings.value: about 10 days at 4 h a day, about 5 days at 8 h a day, backlight at its dimmest
findings.source_title: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 Review (GamePadSquire Test Desk, updated 2026-08-09)
findings.note: GamePadSquire: 4,000 mAh, about 40 hours at the dimmest RGB setting. Arithmetic: 40 / 4 = 10 days; 40 / 8 = 5 days; average draw 4,000 mAh / 40 h = 100 mA. The page does not say whether 40 h is its own measurement or Gamakay's rating, and gives no figure at brighter settings.

findings.label: Reported latency against one report interval
findings.value: about 0.25 ms, equal to 2 report intervals at 8,000 Hz
findings.source_title: Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 Review (GamePadSquire Test Desk, updated 2026-08-09)
findings.note: GamePadSquire says 0.125 ms marketed, 'measured around 0.25 ms'. Arithmetic: 0.25 / 0.125 = 2. Weak input: the page names no tester and no method for the latency figure (it cites Keyboard Inspector only for polling). Do not use it to rank boards.

findings.label: Lab latency for budget boards on a cited rival page
findings.value: MCHOSE Ace 68: 0.3 ms (HLPlanet, measured with OSLTT); no figure for the NS68, Aula WIN60 HE or MCHOSE Ace 60
findings.source_title: Best Keyboards w/ Hall Effect magnetic switches [2026 GUIDE]
findings.note: Shows what the cited rival already has. HLPlanet lists the NS68 at $42.99, the Aula WIN60 HE at $39.99 and the MCHOSE Ace 60 (not the Pro) at $49.99 with 'very low latency' and no number. The Ace 60 Pro, HE68 Lite, WIN68 HE and K617 HE are not on that page.
